evidence: Clear module separation by backend (es/elastic/, es/opendistro/, es/tests/, utils/), with no explicit inter-service communication mechanisms (e.g., no HTTP client patterns for remote services)
Shared abstractions in es/baseapi.py and es/basesqlalchemy.py reused across Elastic and OpenDistro implementations—indicating cohesion within a single deployable unit
No evidence of bounded contexts with separate deployments, service meshes, or API gateways typical of microservices
Directory depth limited to 4, and 5 packages total—consistent with a well-structured monolith rather than distributed system
Test suite resides inside the main module (es/tests/) rather than being in a separate repository/service, reinforcing single-deployment model
All API dialects (Elastic, OpenDistro) share a common DBAPI and SQLAlchemy adapter layer—classic modularization pattern within a monolith
risks: Tight coupling between database dialect implementations and shared base classes could hinder independent evolution of Elastic vs. OpenDistro support
Lack of explicit dependency inversion (e.g., no clearly defined ports/interfaces decoupled from infrastructure) may reduce testability and test isolation beyond current unit test mocks
Shared exception hierarchy used across dialects may leak implementation details or obscure source of errors
